The lithosphere is about 100 km thick and floats on the asthenosphere.
The asthenosphere is a weaker, more viscous layer that allows movement.
The crust is the thin outermost layer and is divided into oceanic and continental crust.
Oceanic crust is thinner and denser, made mostly of basalt, and forms ocean basins.
The thinnest oceanic crust is at the Marianas Trench.
Continental crust is thicker but less dense, made mostly of granite, and thickest at Mt. E
Differences in asthenosphere movement cause the lithosphere to crack into tectonic plates.

There are nine major lithospheric plates, with the Pacific Plate as the largest.
The Philippine Plate is considered a minor plate.
Tectonic activities shape Earth's geological features.
